specName: Identifier-First Sign-In and a Faster Launch
last_action: Stopped after the verified Foundational slice; the spec is left at implementing.
expectations: Moving or removing visual-priming is out of scope; it must stay last before hand-over
Machine setup, the blocked surface and the shell behaviour are unchanged except where named
No cache refresh call may be added to the application
The identifier enumeration vector is accepted, not fixed
context: constraint: every wait has a stated maximum (30s ceiling)
constraint: every data operation goes through a stored procedure with paired rollback
constraint: roles come from the store only; no local override or mock mode

FR-001.title: Sign-in collects an identifier, then a credential

FR-002.title: Exactly four digits is an employee number; anything else a user name

FR-003.title: An employee number is looked up in the store first

FR-004.title: When the store lacks the number, look it up in the plant system

FR-005.title: A store-recognised person proceeds to the PIN stage, unchanged after that

FR-006.title: A plant-system person the store lacks is offered the set-up panel

FR-007.title: The set-up panel shows the plant-system name, prefilled and editable

FR-008.title: The set-up panel asks for the PIN twice under the existing rules

FR-009.title: Creation bypasses default PIN 4330, so no temporary credential

FR-010.title: A created account holds the lowest rank, read from the store

FR-011.title: The set-up panel says a higher level needs IT

FR-012.title: A person in neither source is refused plainly and the form stays open

FR-013.title: Unreachable plant system with no mirror record refuses, never guesses

FR-014.title: Enter submits, and on set-up advances then submits at the end

FR-015.title: A blank field shows its hint rather than doing nothing

FR-016.title: Splash, sign-in, setup and blocked become stages of one window

FR-017.title: That window hosts the launch then becomes the shell

FR-018.title: The navigation panel is hidden while the launch runs

FR-019.title: The window maximises on hand-over to the shell

FR-020.title: The window re-centres after each resize it makes

FR-021.title: The window opens centred on the screen it starts on

FR-022.title: The shell is reachable only from the main-screens outcome

FR-023.title: Nothing assumes a signed-in person before the hand-over

FR-024.title: A launch-wide budget of about 45 seconds to shell or stated stop

FR-025.title: The budget is additional to every step's own stated maximum

FR-026.title: The three session checks run together

FR-027.title: The local reads run alongside the first store contact

FR-028.title: The picture cache starts at the beginning of the launch

FR-029.title: The external-system priming stays last before the hand-over

FR-030.title: The application never triggers a cached-data refresh

FR-031.title: The surface shows several operations while each keeps its own line

FR-032.title: A sixth read shape returns an employee by number with cached fallback

FR-033.title: The shape-count test and the ruleset are updated to six

FR-034.title: One procedure creates profile, credential and rank, with rollback

FR-035.title: No shared key file is read, copied or kept; stale docs reported

FR-036.title: Every wait keeps a stated maximum, 30-second ceiling

FR-037.title: A stop states its own cause and offers only fitting remedies

FR-038.title: The pipeline refuses to continue while the machine is unconfigured

FR-039.title: Roles come from the store only

FR-040.title: Every data operation uses a procedure; schema ships rollback

FR-041.title: The replaced launch behaviour does not return

FR-042.title: Nothing is kept on a computer except the local picture copy

FR-043.title: A launch ends at exactly one of five outcomes

FR-044.title: The identifier enumeration vector is accepted and recorded

FR-024a.title: Leaving the set-up panel creates nothing and returns to the identifier stage

FR-045.title: The set-up PIN is an ordinary credential, never temporary

specify.summary: Specify wrote 7 prioritized user stories, 44 functional requirements and 13 success criteria for identifier-first sign-in with self set-up, one launch window, and a faster concurrent launch.
specify.key_finding: The store already exposes an employee-by-identifier read and the profile table already carries an employee identifier column, so stage 1 needs no new store schema.
specify.risks: The sixth read shape is real database and service work; the documentation and the key-file code disagree and must be reconciled.

clarify.summary: Clarify resolved five material ambiguities with informed defaults: inactive accounts, the budget as a hard stop, where the lowest rank comes from, leaving set-up, and the status of the chosen PIN.
clarify.key_finding: No clarification needed user input; each question had a sound default grounded in an existing invariant.
clarify.risks: The enumeration vector remains accepted and unmitigated.

plan.summary: Plan sized the work across four subsystems and settled concurrency, the sixth read shape's ownership, the set-up path, the single window and how a budget overrun is reported.
plan.key_finding: The key-file contradiction is the instruction document being stale: SharedKeyFileSource is registered, RememberedSignInService uses it, and the catalogue still targets 'the shared key file'.
plan.risks: The sixth shape needs a new module value, so the catalog, the folder layout and the count assertions all move together.

tasks.summary: 61 tasks in ten phases: a thirteen-task Foundational wave for the sixth read shape and account creation, then one phase per user story in priority order, then Polish.
tasks.key_finding: The sixth read shape blocks US2, so it sits in Foundational rather than in its own P3 phase.
tasks.risks: Phases 6 and 7 are the riskiest: the window restructure touches App.xaml.cs, and the pipeline concurrency touches the routing walk.

analyze.summary: Analyze found one critical spec-versus-code conflict (the key file) and three medium gaps, with no constitution violation.
analyze.key_finding: FR-042 cannot be true while the existing key-file reader remains; the feature reports it rather than changing behaviour.
analyze.risks: A reviewer must decide whether a later feature withdraws the key-file read.

implement.summary: Implemented the Foundational database and cache slice for the sixth read shape plus the account-creation procedure: 17 of 61 tasks, all verified by the mock and guard test suites.
implement.key_finding: The mock count assertions were partly derived and partly hard-coded; the hard-coded ones needed deliberate updates in four test files.
implement.risks: The sign-in stages, the single window and the concurrent launch are not implemented.

intent: Identifier-first sign-in with self set-up, one launch window, and a faster concurrent launch

decisions.decision: An identifier is an employee number only when it is exactly four digits; every other identifier is a user name.
decisions.why: A shape rule is the only signal available at the identifier stage, and it must be unambiguous.

decisions.decision: An inactive store account holding the employee number is refused and never offered set-up, even when the plant system knows the number.
decisions.why: Creating a second account for a number the store already holds would risk a duplicate identity.

decisions.decision: The launch-wide budget is a hard stop that ends the launch at a stated stop naming the budget.
decisions.why: A budget with no stop would be a wait with no maximum, which the launch path forbids.

decisions.decision: Each step's own stated maximum still applies independently of the launch-wide budget.
decisions.why: The budget must never replace a step's maximum (FR-025).

decisions.decision: The lowest rank is read from the store's own rank list at creation and chosen by the store's ordering.
decisions.why: Roles come from the store only; naming a rank in code would break that invariant.

decisions.decision: Leaving the set-up panel creates nothing and returns the person to the identifier stage.
decisions.why: An abandoned set-up must not leave a partial account.

decisions.decision: The PIN chosen at set-up is an ordinary credential from creation, so the five-attempt temporary-credential rule never applies to it.
decisions.why: Creation bypasses the default PIN, so there is no temporary state to exhaust.

decisions.decision: The external-system priming step stays last before the hand-over and is not moved or removed.
decisions.why: The cached or live verdict must be settled before the shell opens.

decisions.decision: Rejected: allowing the application to trigger a cache refresh during launch.
decisions.why: Refreshing the mirror is the caching service's own job on its own cadence.

decisions.decision: Concurrency is expressed as explicit parallel groups in the pipeline; each member still runs through the existing runner under its own stated maximum.
decisions.why: The runner already owns the per-step bound and the one-terminal-line rule; moving concurrency into it would make the bound harder to verify.
decisions.rejected: A general task graph, or making every step concurrent.

decisions.decision: The sixth read shape gets its own VisualReadShapeModule value whose folder is Module_Startup.
decisions.why: The shape belongs to the launch, and filing it under setup or waitlist would make the catalog lie about ownership.

decisions.decision: Account creation writes the chosen PIN as the stored credential through one new procedure with a non-temporary flag.
decisions.why: The existing temporary-credential and new-PIN logic must not be disturbed, and the spec forbids the temporary-credential state for a self-created account.
decisions.rejected: Creating on the default PIN 4330 and driving the new-PIN path.

decisions.decision: Identifier classification and the two lookups live in a new service, not in the view model.
decisions.why: The classification and its edge cases need exhaustive tests that do not require a window.

decisions.decision: One LaunchWindow hosts stage views; the four surfaces stop being windows.
decisions.why: The spec asks for stages of the main window, and the shell must be the same window that hosted the launch.
decisions.rejected: Keeping four windows and hiding three.

decisions.decision: Several lines at once is a presentation concern over the existing append-only feed.
decisions.why: The feed is already thread-safe, append-only and keyed by step id, so a second collection would only duplicate state that could disagree.

decisions.decision: The key-file contradiction is reported, and the instruction document is corrected to match the code; no behaviour changes.
decisions.why: The code still reads the key file, so the document is the stale side, and the request forbids a silent behaviour change.
decisions.rejected: Deleting the key-file reader to match the document.

decisions.decision: The launch budget is a linked cancellation that ends the walk at Blocked with a cause naming the budget.
decisions.why: A launch must not end on an unnamed wait, and no single step caused the overrun so blaming one would be wrong.
decisions.rejected: Recording the overrun as a step failure.

decisions.decision: picture-cache moves to the first catalogue position; visual-priming stays last before shell.
decisions.why: Starting the best-effort cache first removes end-of-launch waiting, and the priming verdict must be settled before the shell opens.
decisions.rejected: Running the picture cache concurrently with everything.

decisions.decision: sp_core_account_setup_create reads the lowest rank itself and writes the credential as non-temporary.
decisions.why: No caller may name a rank, and the person must never enter the temporary-credential state.
decisions.rejected: Passing a rank in, or creating on the default PIN 4330.

approach: Sign-in becomes two stages with a new identifier service resolving store-first then plant-system; one LaunchWindow hosts the launch stages then becomes the shell; the pipeline gains parallel groups plus a 45-second budget on top of each step's maximum, and a sixth cached read shape serves the employee lookup.

concerns.note: FR-042 and FR-035 assert that nothing but the picture copy is kept on a machine, but the code reads a shared key file for remembered sign-in. The behaviour is left unchanged by this feature and the instruction document is corrected instead.
Where a self-created account's user name comes from is unspecified; settled at implement time by an informed default (derived from the confirmed name, unique in the store).
The 'several lines at once' surface contract is not precise enough to test; settled at implement time as one line per started-and-not-ended operation with no history.
The concurrency group boundaries live in the contract rather than in the spec's requirement text.
The spec alternates between 'PIN stage' and 'credential stage' for the same stage.
The task list has no Phase 1 because there is no setup work to do.
'read-computer-record' and 'read-machine-configuration' correctly belong to neither concurrency group.

17 of 61 tasks are implemented and verified. The Foundational database and cache slice is complete; every task from T012 onward is not started. The spec is deliberately left at implementing rather than implemented.

The task-close timestamps for T001 to T020 were stamped in bursts when the work was already finished, so the durations are a recording artifact rather than the real build time. The work itself is real and verified.

A new account's user name is the upper-cased confirmed name with spaces removed, and a duplicate is refused by MySQL's own duplicate-key error. This was analysis A2, settled here by an informed default.
sp_core_account_setup_create writes no audit row, because the act has no actor. This departs from sp_user_management_create deliberately and is recorded in analysis.md A2.
The sixth read shape's mirror tables and procedures have not been applied to a real store in this session; only their files and the catalog-driven validation are verified.
